name: clear_field_44_bytes_in
description: Writes a zero longword into a field 44 bytes past a base pointer held in a register, then returns. The routine is called from one other routine and touches nothing else.

key: final fight (1991)(u. s. gold)[cr csl][t +3 slipstream](disk 1 of 2)/Final Fight (1991)(U. S. Gold)[cr CSL][t +3 Slipstream](Disk 1 of 2).adf:bootblock:0:0276
name: call_libraries_walk_records
description: Calls several Amiga library routines through a base pointer, stores two constants into the structures they return, then walks a zero-terminated table of records and calls two more library routines for each record. The final step stores a saved register value into a field of the base structure.

name: open_close_library_permit_sequence
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The listed facts show a 29-instruction routine that opens a library, closes a library, and calls the exec Permit routine, and it is entered from outside the static flow.

name: call_six_routines_in_order
description: Makes six consecutive calls to other routines and then returns, with no data handling of its own. It is reached from one caller and through a program-counter-relative address reference.

name: initialise_paired_table_entries
description: Loops eight times over two tables spaced eight bytes apart, writing one constant 16-bit value into offset 6 and the number 5 into offset 2 of each entry. The two tables are fixed addresses and no other inputs are read.

name: fill_two_tables_stepping_values
description: Writes fixed values into a few single fields, then loops three times, writing the low and high words of a value into the paired tables at each step. The value advances by 682 on each pass.

name: reset_copper_and_dma_registers
description: Forbids multitasking, calls a routine through a library offset, saves the DMA control value, then writes to the copper location registers, the DMA and interrupt enable registers, and a CIA port. The listing shows the copper and DMA setup, but the exact enable sequence depends on which bits the writes set.

name: build_xor_sequence_table
description: Writes six pointer-and-count entries into a table, calls a routine five times, then fills twenty-four pairs of words with a value that is XOR-mixed from a global byte and advanced on each step, ending the table with a zero word.

name: fill_xor_sequence_from_pointer
description: Fills a table from a caller-supplied pointer with twenty-four pairs of words, each mixed with a global byte and advanced by a fixed step, then writes a zero terminator. Its only hardware reference is a custom-chip offset that is read as an input.

name: zero_fill_2156_longwords
description: Zeroes a block of 2156 longwords starting at a fixed address, using a simple countdown loop, and returns.

name: zero_fill_4334_longwords
description: Zeroes a second fixed block of 4334 longwords with the same countdown loop as the routine before it, and returns.

name: run_endless_loop_with_title
description: Runs an endless loop that calls one routine on each pass and never returns. The listing references the title text FINAL FIGHT, and the other routines it calls are reached only through this loop.

name: toggle_flag_and_poll_counter
description: Clears a byte at an address supplied in a register, flips a global flag between zero and all bits set, then calls a routine repeatedly until a counter register reads three.

name: poll_flag_counter_alt
description: Clears a byte at an address supplied in a register, flips a global flag between zero and all bits set, then calls a routine repeatedly until a counter register reads three. The code is identical to the neighbouring routine, and it is called from one caller.

name: toggle_flag_shared_poll_entry
description: Clears a byte at an address supplied in a register, flips a global flag between zero and all bits set, then calls a routine repeatedly until a counter register reads three. Three different callers reach this entry point, so it is the shared form of the same sequence.

name: forward_call_to_one_routine
description: Makes a single call to another routine and returns, passing nothing of its own.

name: copy_character_glyph_rows
description: Reads a character from a string through a register index, skipping zero bytes and the end marker. It then copies seven bytes from a table, indexed by the character code minus 32, into an output buffer at intervals of 88 bytes.

name: add_offsets_to_three_tables
description: Adds one, two and three to bytes of three interleaved tables at a stride of eight bytes, once over thirteen entries and then again over twenty-four entries.

name: write_nop_pattern_when_set
description: Checks a global byte three times, and whenever it is nonzero stores a value made of two 68000 no-operation instruction words into a global longword. The stored value disables whatever code or data it is later written over.

name: reset_audio_periods_and_flags
description: Zeroes the period registers of the four audio channels, then stores 15 in a global control value and clears its second bit. The listing references the audio registers and the control-port register, but the port itself is not written here.

name: initialise_channel_records_and_tables
description: Sets a global flag bit and several table base values, then copies nine groups of values into a record block, derives eight running offsets, and fills eighty entries of pointer and length fields. It finishes by setting the audio pointer register and writing the interrupt and DMA enable registers.

name: update_audio_channels_each_frame
description: Runs each frame when a playback flag is set. It counts down a tempo counter, calls four routines when it reaches zero, writes the four audio channel registers through routine calls, and sets the DMA enable bit in a global word. For each channel it counts down a timer and, when the count falls from two to one, reloads that channel's sample pointer and length registers.

name: advance_channel_sequence_step
description: Advances one channel's playback state. When the step counter has run out it reads the next command bytes from a sequence, updates the channel's position and loads new values, otherwise it applies the current command bits to the channel record and sets the channel's DMA bit.

name: interpret_sequence_command_bytes
description: Loops over a byte sequence for one channel until its stop flag is set, interpreting negative-coded command bytes. Some commands load a stored value into the channel record and write it out, some jump to another offset in the sequence, and one checks a four-character tag in a referenced block before reading an embedded sequence.

name: stub_decompile_timeout_call_pair
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The listed facts show a 10-instruction routine entered through a program-counter-relative address reference, which calls two other routines and is called from one caller.

name: stub_decompile_timeout_ports
description: Pseudo-code is unavailable because decompilation timed out. The listed facts show a 104-instruction routine that touches the joystick and fire-button port, the second CIA port and a custom-chip register, and makes two calls.

name: clear_state_bit_after_delay
description: If bit three of a global state byte is set, it busy-waits through a countdown of about 100 steps, clears bit six of that byte, and then sets the byte to eight. The listed facts also mention CIA and interrupt request registers, which the pseudo-code does not show being written.

name: call_four_routines_when_flagged
description: When bit five of a global state byte is set, it makes four calls to other routines and then resets the byte to that bit value. The facts add that it touches the interrupt request register and a custom-chip register.

name: advance_stepped_global_counter
description: If a global value is zero it steps it up by 273 and wraps it to one once it reaches 4095. Otherwise it counts the value down by one.

name: render_text_glyphs_on_counter
description: Runs only when the low nibble of a global counter equals fourteen. It copies two blocks of 230 longwords and one block of 60 words between fixed regions, then for each character of a text string it looks up a glyph position from the character code minus 32, shifts the glyph bits into a row buffer, and copies the rows to the output region.

name: step_state_nibble_and_wrap
description: Decrements a global state byte by 32 in total. When its high nibble reaches the wrap value it sets the state to one, keeps the saved value, and writes two words at fixed offsets from that saved value.

name: count_down_copy_row_bands
description: Decrements a counter and, when it reaches zero, resets it to 100 and restores a saved source pointer. It then copies two bands of rows, each twenty-three rows of twenty-one words, from the source into a fixed destination buffer.

name: clear_memory_set_system_registers
description: Zeroes a block of 8832 longwords at a fixed address, then writes fixed values into global words and into the copper, DMA and interrupt registers, including two routine addresses. It is called from two places.

name: allocate_and_configure_boot
description: Boot-block entry point. It calls the exec memory allocator through a library, sets fields in the returned structure, then calls one library routine up to three times to pick a size and a matching count. It then loops over the bits of a stored word, calling routines and adjusting a counter for each set bit.

key: leander (1991)(psygnosis)(disk 1 of 3)[cr skr][t +8 legend]/Leander (1991)(Psygnosis)(Disk 1 of 3)[cr SKR][t +8 Legend].adf:bootblock:0:0100
name: send_io_request_wait_status
description: Sends a request through the exec device I/O call and then waits in an empty loop until a status bit clears, after which it runs a closing routine. The listed facts show it reading a bit of the CIA-A port register, which carries the joystick and disk status.

key: leander (1991)(psygnosis)(disk 1 of 3)[cr skr][t +8 legend]/Leander (1991)(Psygnosis)(Disk 1 of 3)[cr SKR][t +8 Legend].adf:bootblock:0:0200
name: open_graphics_and_init_copper
description: Opens the graphics library by name and calls two library routines. It sets a copper-list pointer, clears eighty longwords at a fixed address, and copies thirty longwords from a source into a buffer. The referenced text includes a title string and the graphics library name.

key: leander (1991)(psygnosis)(disk 1 of 3)[cr skr][t +8 legend]/Leander (1991)(Psygnosis)(Disk 1 of 3)[cr SKR][t +8 Legend].adf:bootblock:0:0292
name: copy_long_clear_word
description: Copies a longword from one structure into a field 128 bytes into another structure, then clears a word field 136 bytes further along. Both pointers are supplied in registers.

name: count_global_down_full_cycle
description: Writes successive words to a global variable, counting down from minus one through every 16-bit value until it wraps back to minus one, then returns minus one. The listed facts note a background-colour register touch, which the pseudo-code does not show.

name: run_nine_step_frame_loop
description: Runs an endless loop that calls nine routines in order on each pass. A global value is checked against a threshold and selects one of two branches, and both branches call routines and wait while a bit of a global byte is set. The facts add that it touches the joystick and disk status port.

name: select_adkcon_mode_and_write
description: Clears several state words, copies a hardware register value into one of them, and chooses one of two routine calls by testing a passed-in value against 1 and 6. It then writes a bit-15-set value derived from that register to the audio and disk control register.

name: set_port_and_check_tag
description: Calls several routines, saves an input pointer, and sets the second CIA port register to all ones. If a four-character tag at the saved pointer matches a fixed value it calls one more routine, then clears a word field and returns.

name: search_record_table_for_key
description: Stores two pointers in a structure and calls one routine, then scans up to 128 records spaced 32 bytes apart for a matching first longword. It sets a status word to zero when the key is found and to minus one when an end marker is reached or the search runs out, then writes all ones to the second CIA port.

name: find_name_in_table
description: Compares a name against consecutive 32-byte table entries, ignoring letter case, and moves on to the next entry at each mismatch. On a match it stores a longword from the entry at offset 28 in a global and returns the longword at offset 24.

name: save_copy_restore_scratch_block
description: Saves a 60-byte block of code or data into a buffer, copies a region whose length is held in a global variable, calls routines, and then writes the saved 60 bytes back. The listing does not resolve the routines it calls.

name: unpack_packed_block_backwards
description: If the block's header tag is not PP20, it copies the block byte by byte backwards. Otherwise it unpacks the block, reading control bits and copying literal bytes and repeated runs from the end of the buffer toward the start.

name: unpack_packed_block_pcrel_entry
description: Shares the same unpacking code as its neighbours, reached here through a program-counter-relative address. It checks the PP20 header tag, copies unpacked bytes backwards from the end of the buffer, and returns.

name: unpack_packed_block_secondary
description: Shares the same PP20 unpacking code as its neighbours and is called from two places. It reads control bits, copies literal bytes and back-reference runs backwards through the buffer, and calls four routines to fetch and write the data.

name: test_upper_bits_then_return
description: Shifts a register right by one and tests whether the result is nonzero, then returns in either case. Both branches return straight away, so the routine has no observable effect.

name: shift_out_bits_from_stream
description: Shifts single bits out of a bit register one at a time, loading the next 32-bit word from memory whenever the register runs empty. It repeats for a count held in a register.

name: split_size_and_copy_loop
description: Stores a pointer and a size, splits the size into a quotient and remainder by 5632, and then calls routines in a loop until a stored pointer is reached. The facts add that it touches the second CIA port and a custom-chip register.

name: set_control_bit_when_clear
description: When bit zero of a word at offset 12 in the supplied structure is clear, it clears bit one and sets bit zero of a control byte, then calls a routine.

name: pulse_bit_while_status_set
description: Writes a control value to a byte at the supplied pointer, clearing bit three and setting bit one. It then toggles bit zero and calls a routine repeatedly for as long as a status bit at a fixed offset from that pointer stays set.

name: pulse_bit_count_halved_times
description: Clears bit one of a control byte, then halves a word read from the structure and toggles bit zero once per step, calling a routine on each step, until the count reaches zero.

name: configure_then_wait_for_ready
description: Writes fixed control bytes to four device registers and sets one bit in another, then busy-waits until bit zero of the first register reads as set.

name: copy_sector_bytes_to_buffer
description: Sets or clears bit two of a control byte according to bit zero of a structure word, then calls a routine. It splits a position value into a 512-byte sector number and an offset, finds the matching sector in a table, and copies bytes from it into a destination buffer until the end count of 5632 is reached.

name: decode_mfm_disk_sector
description: Starts a floppy disk read by setting the disk sync word and disk pointer registers and enabling DMA. It then scans for sync words and decodes the interleaved odd and even bit fields of each block into a buffer while accumulating an XOR checksum.

name: unpack_packed_stream_runs
description: Decodes a bit-packed stream read from the end of a buffer. Control bits choose between copying literal bytes and repeating earlier output from a run-length table, and the output is written through a pointer. It calls one routine before finishing.

name: decode_bit_counts_copy_runs
description: Reads bit-packed counts from the end of the input, then in a loop copies runs of bytes backwards within the output buffer, using the decoded count as each run length, until the stream ends.

name: forward_single_routine_call
description: Calls one other routine and returns straight away, adding nothing of its own.

name: chain_six_routine_calls
description: Calls another routine six times in sequence and returns, with no other work.

name: poll_until_zero_then_call
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then calls a second routine and returns.

name: poll_then_call_four_routines
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, makes one fixed call, then calls four further routines in turn and returns.

name: poll_routine_then_fixed_call
description: Calls a routine once and, if it returns zero, makes a fixed call and returns. Otherwise it keeps calling the routine until it returns zero, then makes the same fixed call and returns.

name: poll_routine_fixed_call_alt
description: Has the same code as its neighbouring routine: it polls a routine until it returns zero, then makes a fixed call. It is called from one caller.

name: poll_routine_unreached_copy
description: Has the same code as the routines around it, and is reached only by decoding a gap in the file as code. It polls a routine until it returns zero, then makes a fixed call.

name: poll_routine_then_two_calls
description: Calls a routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then makes two fixed calls and returns.

name: repeat_routine_in_timed_rounds
description: Sets a counter to 63 and, for each count, waits until a global value reads minus one, then calls a routine 32 times. The facts list the vertical beam position register as touched, but the listed code shows only the global wait.

name: count_up_routine_rounds
description: Counts a global value up from zero to 64. For each step it waits until a global reads minus one and then calls a routine 32 times. The facts list the vertical beam position register as touched, but the listed code shows only the global wait.

name: wait_for_flag_then_halt
description: Waits until a global value reads minus two, then enters an endless loop that never returns. The facts list the vertical beam position register as touched, which the listed code does not show.

name: lookup_nibbles_into_word
description: Takes a 16-bit value, splits three nibbles out of it, looks each up in a byte table at a computed base, combines the results into one word and stores that word through a pointer.

name: setup_blitter_and_clear_buffer
description: Copies eight longwords from a fixed source to a destination, clears 10000 longwords at a fixed address, advances a wrapping counter, and writes constants to global variables that the facts map to blitter registers. It finishes by setting a flag to one.

name: wait_flag_set_values
description: Waits until a global value equals minus 112, then writes three fixed values to global variables. The facts list the copper, DMA and beam position registers as touched.

name: install_vector_and_enable_irqs
description: Stores the address of a routine into a global vector slot, then writes a constant with bit 15 set to the interrupt-enable register, which enables the interrupt sources it selects.

name: handle_interrupt_flag_bits
description: Checks bits of a global state word. When bit five is set it resets the word to that bit and calls routines if a related flag is set. Otherwise it sets a new state value depending on bit four. The facts show the interrupt request register and a custom-chip register touched.

name: clear_and_copy_work_buffers
description: Clears ten thousand longwords at one fixed address, then copies seventy longwords from one buffer into another. The listing continues with pointer and bit manipulation over further tables, which the output truncates.
